Kadai.reason: Kadai appears only in “Tai–Kadai,” the name of a language family, not a human language; therefore false_positive.

Nasal.reason: Nasal refers to a class of speech sounds and codas, not a human language; therefore false_positive.

English.reason: English is referred to as a human language and a source of orthographic conventions, but only as a design precedent; therefore mentioned_only.

Pinyin.reason: Pinyin is explicitly a romanization scheme for Standard Chinese, not a human language; therefore false_positive.

Rom.reason: Rom is used as an abbreviation for romanization in the table headers “Thai Rom” and “Lao Rom,” not as a language name; therefore false_positive.

Korean.reason: Korean is named as the language associated with Revised Romanization and the vowel ɯ, but only as a romanization precedent; therefore mentioned_only.

Japanese.reason: Japanese is mentioned only as a source of romanization precedents for representing a vowel; therefore mentioned_only.

Lao.reason: Lao is one of the two target languages for which the paper designs a romanization scheme; therefore studied.

Thai.reason: Thai is one of the two target languages for which the paper designs a romanization scheme; therefore studied.

Latin.reason: Latin refers to the Latin alphabet, letters, and script-based orthographies, not the Latin language; therefore false_positive.

Vietnamese.reason: Vietnamese is named for its VIQR transcription system and letter ư as a romanization precedent, without any work on Vietnamese itself; therefore mentioned_only.

Chinese.reason: Chinese refers to Chinese users and to Standard or Yue Chinese as context for Pinyin correspondence, without experiments or resources for Chinese itself; therefore mentioned_only.
